brief: Calculate tax in a fictional progressive bracket system without applying the top rate to all income.

en-US.scenario: Fictional US-dollar examples for "Tax Brackets"; illustrative amounts, not current prices or product offers. No assumption of salary, bank ownership or spare income.

es-MX.scenario: Ejemplos ficticios en pesos mexicanos para "Calcula cada tramo"; montos ilustrativos, no precios vigentes ni ofertas. No se supone nómina, cuenta bancaria ni dinero sobrante.

pt-BR.scenario: Exemplos fictícios em reais para "Calcule cada faixa"; valores ilustrativos, não preços atuais nem ofertas. Sem supor salário, conta bancária ou dinheiro sobrando.

objective.observable_action: Calculate tax in a fictional progressive bracket system without applying the top rate to all income.
objective.success_criterion: Complete the fresh-context transfer using only its visible information.

instruction.relevance: A higher bracket can apply only to the next slice, not every earlier unit of income.
instruction.misconception: Crossing a progressive bracket applies the highest rate to all income.
instruction.numeracy_support: Use only the visible fictional amounts and conditions; earlier arithmetic is preparation, not a hidden financial assumption.

evidence.reasoning: In this fictional system, each income slice has its own rate. Calculate each slice, then add the tax amounts.
Fictional example: first 100 at 10% owes 10; next 50 at 20% owes 10; Total tax is 20.
You added the taxes on separate income slices.
The stated rule assigns the higher rate only to excess.
Each slice uses its own rate before adding taxes.
The calculator taxes earlier slices at the wrong rate.
The total combines different rates on different slices.
The new thresholds still require separate slice calculations.
